grade_reason: The main point and question are right ($4.88B Sharon backstop, six-year terms, datacenter-lease backstops, class C question), but the article's view that consensus is too low on NVIDIA's 2H revenue is missed, and the announced-deal records name SemiAnalysis on the report day as their original source. That breaks the link to the earlier SharonAI/Firmus announcements and invites double counting. It also has a duplicate pair (e11/e12), a duplicate pair (e17/e18) and a noise record (e16).
standard_doubt: The tier table has no row for a research firm stating a non-public action as fact ('Here, Nvidia is diving even deeper, as it has started backstopping datacenter leases.'); it lands in third_party_view beside pure opinions such as 'The incremental revenue from the backstop program will be significant', so the judge cannot tell a reported action from a view.

The common-knowledge example '融资会是扩大算力最大的障碍' would reject the article's dated claim that the binding constraint moved from datacenters (2025) to chips (early 2026) to financing (mid-2026), which comes from a primary supply-chain tracker and is the premise of NVIDIA's backstop; an analyst might record it as a third-party view, although the backstop facts already carry most of its value.
